findings.semanticClaim: Task capability eligibility was represented in both CAPABILITY_REGISTRY.taskTypes and a second TASK_TYPE_CAPABILITIES map, creating two authority sources despite the documented registry ownership rule.
findings.reproductionStatus: Current source inspection found no TASK_TYPE_CAPABILITIES symbol; deriveTaskCapabilities now reads CAPABILITY_REGISTRY.taskTypes.

findings.semanticClaim: The registry and adapters declared executor identities and typed ports but did not expose concrete non-runtime dispatch end-to-end; only runtime dispatch was visible.
findings.reproductionStatus: Current source contains executeBoundToolOperation with a discriminated switch for Context7, shadcn, Codebase Memory, and Functional QA, followed by registered output conversion.

findings.semanticClaim: Legacy tool normalization was applied at request authorization but not consistently at direct registry lookup/helper boundaries.
findings.reproductionStatus: getToolDefinition and getOperationDefinition now canonicalize IDs, and authority canonicalizes both requests and operation candidates.

findings.semanticClaim: Cross-stage requirement traceability could not be established from the implementation evidence alone; a canonical approved Brief, accepted Planning package, Architecture Review, selected Design, generated TaskGraph identifiers/checksums, and a complete requirement mapping were not evidenced.
findings.reproductionStatus: The current Phase 7B evidence has repository contract checksums and implementation traceability, but no persisted final semantic-review evidence pack and no customer-project Brief/Planning/Design/TaskGraph identity set. The customer-project portion is out of scope; the Phase 7B evidence-persistence gap remains.
findings.rebasedClaim: Persisted Phase 7B review identity, requirement-to-artifact mapping, and current graph/test evidence are incomplete; do not invent customer-project lineage identifiers.

findings.semanticClaim: Non-runtime executor IDs were not connected to executable adapters; adapter code exposed types and IDs but only runtime dispatch was operational.
findings.reproductionStatus: Current adapters.ts dispatches every registered external operation to its typed port and converts the output through registeredOutputToToolResult.

findings.semanticClaim: Authority derived capabilities from allowedTools, allowing a tool permission to become a capability grant instead of deriving task obligations from the registry.
findings.reproductionStatus: deriveTaskCapabilities ignores allowedTools and derives only matching taskTypes from CAPABILITY_REGISTRY; agent and task tool permissions remain separate intersections.

findings.semanticClaim: TaskGraph and developer-tool registry vocabularies differed: the graph emits legacy filesystem/database/npm/shell and aliased Context7/Playwright identifiers while registry validation uses canonical developer-tool IDs.
findings.reproductionStatus: The current architecture documents an explicit compatibility boundary: canonicalToolId covers Context7, Playwright, and ToolRequest aliases; filesystem/database/npm/shell-restricted remain legacy execution-policy IDs and are not developer-tool registry entries.
findings.futurePhaseNote: Migrating every legacy execution-policy identifier into the developer-tool registry would expand authority and is not required by the Phase 7B contract; generic shell/filesystem mutation remains rejected.

findings.semanticClaim: Host executor and workspace authority depended on caller-supplied context without an evidenced authenticity boundary; createToolHostContext accepted caller-provided scope and trusted executor IDs.
findings.reproductionStatus: Static source inspection confirms createToolHostContext is exported, accepts scope and executor identity arrays from its caller, and has no separate host attestation or private host-owned binding. The unique-symbol brand authenticates construction through this exported function, not caller provenance.

findings.semanticClaim: External responses could cause resource work before the bounded ToolResult envelope because output was serialized before the pre-validation size check.
findings.reproductionStatus: Static source inspection confirms JSON.stringify(value) executes before the 200000-byte rejection and before registered output schema validation. Adapter schemas now bound normal outputs, but the public conversion boundary still serializes an arbitrary value before enforcing that bound.
findings.rebasedClaim: The remaining defect is the pre-validation serialization boundary, not the absence of all output limits.

findings.semanticClaim: Source inspection outputs were marked untrusted but lacked centralized redaction, and path policy could expose credentials/config/private-key material.
findings.reproductionStatus: Current output conversion centrally applies redactToolText and current path policy rejects sensitive filenames/extensions including .npmrc, credentials, secrets, id_rsa, private-key names, pem, key, p12, pfx, and der.

findings.semanticClaim: Redaction was limited to fixed environment names and regexes and did not cover common JSON key forms or other credentials.
findings.reproductionStatus: The regex now covers more token/private-key forms, but serialized JSON such as {"password":"value"} is not guaranteed to match the PASSWORD key alternative because the quoted JSON key is not handled. Configured secret replacement remains a fixed environment-name list.

findings.semanticClaim: Runtime dispatch tests checked only that a result passed and commandType was truthy rather than proving operation-to-method mapping.
findings.reproductionStatus: Current tests track calls and assert each operation maps to the expected validator method and commandType.

findings.semanticClaim: The registered Playwright functional-QA operation was not behaviorally demonstrated with a valid report and rejection of an invalid report.
findings.reproductionStatus: Current tests construct a valid FunctionalQaReport, convert it successfully as UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL, and assert invalid output is rejected.

findings.semanticClaim: Tests manually constructed tasks and did not verify the generated TaskGraph path and legacy normalization together.
findings.reproductionStatus: The current focused test still constructs a task directly and exercises resolveTools/validateToolPolicy; it does not invoke the generated TaskGraph builder. It does cover canonical functional aliases and registry-derived task capabilities, so the remaining gap is graph-level evidence rather than missing tool behavior.
findings.rebasedClaim: Add evidence for the actual generated graph-to-tool-policy path without changing the legacy compatibility boundary.

normalizedFindings.canonicalClaim: The exported host-context constructor validates shape and registered executor IDs but does not establish caller provenance or host attestation.
normalizedFindings.rootCauseHypothesis: Factory host authority is represented as caller-provided data plus a local brand rather than as a host-owned binding.
normalizedFindings.affectedAuthorityBoundary: host scope and trusted executor authorization
normalizedFindings.deterministicProofNeeded: Only a host-owned binding can create usable context; unregistered or caller-forged authority cannot authorize an operation.
normalizedFindings.semanticProofNeeded: Security and Architecture reviewers agree the provenance boundary is explicit and cannot be supplied by the agent or arbitrary integration caller.

normalizedFindings.canonicalClaim: External output reaches JSON serialization and regex redaction before all resource and secret-key bounds are enforced.
normalizedFindings.rootCauseHypothesis: The result adapter treats serialization as a harmless prelude, while the trust boundary requires bounded parsing/redaction before arbitrary output is materialized into the result envelope.
normalizedFindings.affectedAuthorityBoundary: external integration output to UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL ToolResult
normalizedFindings.deterministicProofNeeded: Oversized, deeply nested, cyclic, and JSON-key secret inputs fail safely without an unbounded pre-validation serialization step and produce bounded redacted results.
normalizedFindings.semanticProofNeeded: Security, Code/Integration, and Test/Quality reviewers agree the output contract is both bounded and correctly marked untrusted.

normalizedFindings.canonicalClaim: Phase 7B has implementation traceability but lacks a persisted final review identity and direct generated-graph evidence tying the Phase 7B requirements to current artifacts/tests.
normalizedFindings.rootCauseHypothesis: Implementation evidence was assembled independently of the final semantic execution and focused tests exercised policy helpers rather than the actual graph construction path.
normalizedFindings.deterministicProofNeeded: Persist review identity/checksums and exercise the generated graph path with assertions for capabilities, aliases, permissions, and denied tools.
normalizedFindings.semanticProofNeeded: Contract Auditor and Test/Quality Reviewer accept the evidence pack as current, complete, and non-synthetic.
normalizedFindings.futurePhaseOverlap: Customer-project Brief/Planning/Design lineage is not in scope for this factory-only Phase 7B reconciliation.

rootCauseGroups.deterministicReproduction: Source inspection shows the exported createToolHostContext is the only constructor and accepts all authority inputs from its caller.

rootCauseGroups.title: Bound and redact external results before arbitrary materialization
rootCauseGroups.rootCause: The conversion boundary serializes and regex-redacts an arbitrary external value before all resource and JSON-key secret protections are guaranteed.
rootCauseGroups.deterministicReproduction: registeredOutputToToolResult calls JSON.stringify(value) before the 200000-byte rejection and the structured output schema; the redaction expression is not JSON-key aware for quoted keys such as password.
requiredChecks: Oversized and cyclic values fail safely
JSON-key and token-shaped secrets are redacted
rollbackCriteria: The bound depends on an unbounded stringify or parser
Secrets remain in structured or preview output
Any adapter bypasses registered output conversion
